questions.question_text:
Three pieces of cord measure $45\text{ mm}$, $18\text{ cm}$ and $0.6\text{ m}$.
What is their total length in millimetres?

options.why: Added $18$ directly as millimetres instead of converting $18\text{ cm}$ to $180\text{ mm}$.
Converted $0.6\text{ m}$ to $60\text{ mm}$ instead of $600\text{ mm}$.
Left out the $0.6\text{ m}$ piece and added only $45+180$.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Add all three cord lengths in millimetres.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
$18\text{ cm}=180\text{ mm}$.
$0.6\text{ m}=600\text{ mm}$.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
$45+180+600=825\text{ mm}$.

options.why: Left out the $1.4\text{ m}$ side after converting the other two sides to centimetres.
Left out the $75\text{ cm}$ side and added only $140+95$.
Left out the $950\text{ mm}$ side and added only $140+75$.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Add all three triangle sides in centimetres.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
$1.4\text{ m}=140\text{ cm}$.
$950\text{ mm}=95\text{ cm}$.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
$140+75+95=310\text{ cm}$.

options.why: Added one length and one width, $230+65$, instead of counting both pairs of sides.
Counted the two $230\text{ cm}$ lengths but omitted both $65\text{ cm}$ widths.
Counted one $230\text{ cm}$ length and both $65\text{ cm}$ widths, omitting the opposite length.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Count both pairs of rectangle sides in centimetres.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
$2.3\text{ m}=230\text{ cm}$.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
$230+65=295\text{ cm}$.
$2\times295=590\text{ cm}$.

options.why: Subtracted only the $160\text{ cm}$ side from $580\text{ cm}$ and ignored the other known sides.
Subtracted $125+95$ from $580$ but omitted the known $160\text{ cm}$ side.
Added the $380\text{ cm}$ of known sides to the $580\text{ cm}$ perimeter instead of subtracting.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Subtract the known sides from the perimeter in centimetres.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
$5.8\text{ m}=580\text{ cm}$.
$1.6\text{ m}=160\text{ cm}$.
$950\text{ mm}=95\text{ cm}$.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
$160+125+95=380\text{ cm}$.
$x=580-380=200\text{ cm}$.

questions.question_text:
The width of a rectangle is $7.4\text{ cm}$. Its length is $3.8\text{ cm}$ longer than its width.
What is its perimeter?

options.why: Counted only the two $11.2\text{ cm}$ lengths and omitted both widths.
Added one length and one width, $11.2+7.4$, instead of counting both pairs of sides.
Used $4\times7.4$ as if the rectangle were a square and ignored the extra length.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Find the length, then count both pairs of rectangle sides.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
Both measurements are in centimetres.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
Length: $7.4+3.8=11.2\text{ cm}$.
$11.2+7.4=18.6\text{ cm}$.
$2\times18.6=37.2\text{ cm}$.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular arena has perimeter $0.74\text{ km}$ and length $210\text{ m}$.
What is its width?

options.why: Found the width as $160\text{ m}$ and then doubled it unnecessarily.
Subtracted one $210\text{ m}$ length from the full $740\text{ m}$ perimeter instead of halving first.
Divided the perimeter by four as if all four sides of the rectangle were equal.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Half the rectangle perimeter is one length plus one width.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
$0.74\text{ km}=740\text{ m}$.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
$740\div2=370\text{ m}$.
$370-210=160\text{ m}$.
The width is $160\text{ m}$.

questions.question_text:
A five-sided garden has boundary lengths $1.75\text{ m}$, $135\text{ cm}$, $800\text{ mm}$, $1.45\text{ m}$ and $120\text{ cm}$.
What is its perimeter in metres?

options.why: Left out the $800\text{ mm}$ side, which is $0.8\text{ m}$.
Left out the $135\text{ cm}$ side, which is $1.35\text{ m}$.
Counted the $135\text{ cm}$ side twice, adding an extra $1.35\text{ m}$.

questions.solution_text:
**Identify the lengths and what the question asks.**
Add all five garden sides; give metres.

**Change the lengths to the same unit.**
$135\text{ cm}=1.35\text{ m}$.
$800\text{ mm}=0.8\text{ m}$.
$120\text{ cm}=1.2\text{ m}$.

**Calculate the required length or compare the results, then check the answer.**
$1.75+1.35+0.8+1.45+1.2=6.55\text{ m}$.
